sentences.text:
The challenge in this Crl.M.C is against the FIR and further proceedings in Crime No.248/CR/EOW-II/KTM/11 (earlier Crime No.250 of 2011 registered at the Kalady Police Station)
for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 5 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act.

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. When the matter was taken up for consideration, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the final report, arraying the petitioner as an accused was filed in court, but the same was returned noting certain defects.
It is the submission of the learned Public Prosecutor that the Investigating Officer will be resubmitting the final report, after curing the defects, without delay.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the crime is of the year 2011 and even going by the submission of the Public Prosecutor, the final report has not been accepted by the court.
It is contended that the inordinate delay in completing the investigation, by itself, is a ground for quashing the 2025:KER:74429 CRL.MC NO. 3357 OF 2021 proceedings.
4. Having heard the learned counsel on both sides, this Court is also of the opinion that there cannot be further delay in filing the final report.

The Crl.M.C is hence disposed of with the following directions;
i) The Investigating Officer in Crime No.248/CR/EOW-II/ KTM/11 (earlier Crime No.250 of 2011 of Kalady Police Station) shall resubmit the final report, after curing the defects, within six weeks.
ii) Once the resubmitted final report is accepted, the learned Magistrate shall take earnest efforts to conduct trial and dispose of the case at the earliest.

Sd/-
